claims.statement: The claims manual is internal process direction: coverage and claim obligations must be taken from the applicable policy, endorsement, bulletin, or law, and internal thresholds or procedures cannot create coverage or replace contract terms.

Policy assembly is edition- and attachment-specific: the Mississippi HO-3 2018-09 edition remains in force for policies written under it even though it is superseded for policies effective on or after 2024-03-01, while the Florida HO 01 09 endorsement forms part of the policy and controls over conflicting policy language.

Claim intake opens a file on receipt of loss information, records the source and reported facts, verifies reporting authority, acknowledges receipt without a coverage promise, and preserves a chronological record of material communications and actions.

Claim evaluation must keep coverage, causation, scope or valuation, and payment authority distinct; inspections, estimates, proofs of loss, payments, and appraisal do not by themselves resolve every issue.

Material complexity, disputed coverage or causation, legal or regulatory contact, catastrophe exposure, governmental or code involvement, fraud or recovery indicators, unusual valuation, and other specialized triggers require factual escalation while ordinary supported claim activity continues under authorized direction.

The manual's referral amounts are internal authority controls: it requires referral above $25,000 generally and above $50,000 for catastrophe exposure before commitments beyond delegated authority, and those amounts are not policy limits or customer deadlines.

Proof of loss handling is contract-specific and evidence-based: the handler requests material information, reviews completeness without treating the submission as coverage acceptance, compares it with claim evidence, preserves the record, and pays an authorized undisputed covered amount without waiting for an unrelated dispute.

The Mississippi HO-3 2024-03 conditions require a signed sworn proof of loss within 90 days after request, while the Florida HO 01 09 2023-07 endorsement identifies a sworn-proof deadline but directs the applicable duty to the endorsement and policy; the Mississippi period cannot be generalized to Florida.

Appraisal addresses the amount of a covered loss rather than coverage, policy interpretation, causation, or policy-condition compliance; under Mississippi HO-3 2024-03, appraisers are selected within 30 days, the award states amount and actual cash value, and payment follows the form's specified agreement, judgment, or appraisal-award trigger.

Suit handling requires prompt referral and preservation, and the Mississippi HO-3 2024-03 form requires an insured to commence an action within two years after the date of loss after complying with policy conditions; other forms or applicable law may differ.

Prompt-payment controls are jurisdiction- and form-specific: Florida HO 01 09 2023-07 provides an 85-business-day accept-or-reject period after requested items and a 20-business-day payment period after acceptance, while Mississippi HO-3 2024-03 uses a 60-day payment condition tied to agreement, judgment, or appraisal award.

Texas and North Carolina bulletins require prompt, reasonable, contract-based claim handling, clear explanations, records supporting material decisions, and payment of undisputed amounts when due, but they do not supply a universal replacement for the operative policy's deadlines and conditions.

Catastrophe operations use an event designation and common identifier, prioritize safety and emergency mitigation, preserve evidence, use alternate inspection methods when access is unsafe, reconcile payments and files, and continue ordinary claim obligations after event operations close.

Under Mississippi HO-3 2024-03, ordinance-or-law coverage applies to increased cost necessary to comply with an ordinance or law regulating construction, repair, or demolition of a covered building damaged by a covered cause of loss, is limited to 15 percent of the dwelling amount of insurance, requires the requirement to be in effect when the loss occurs, and separately covers required demolition and reconstruction only when the damaged portion is subject to the requirement; the form excludes pre-loss requirements not enforced because of the loss and elective demolition or reconstruction.

Florida hurricane-deductible administration requires clear, policy-consistent disclosure of the trigger, calculation basis, and relationship to other deductibles, with retained records and correction of material inconsistencies; the bulletin does not authorize applying an unsupported deductible.

Mississippi DP-3 2026-01 has materially different claim controls from the Mississippi HO-3: its Section I exclusion bars loss caused by enforcement of an ordinance or law, proof of loss is due within 60 days after request, appraiser selection is due within 20 days, appraisal determines only amount of loss, payment is due within 30 days after agreement or a final appraisal award, and suit is subject to a two-year condition qualified by applicable law.

North Carolina Bulletin NCDOI-2021-06 requires claim acknowledgment within 30 days after receipt and acceptance or denial within 30 business days after the insurer receives all requested items necessary to evaluate the claim; it also requires reasonable investigation, prompt payment of undisputed amounts when due, clear explanations, and supporting claim records, while the claims manual's 15-day acknowledgment target remains an internal control rather than a substitute for the bulletin or policy.

The North Carolina HO-01-32 form sets contractual claims-handling periods of 30 days to acknowledge a claim, 30 business days after receiving requested decision materials to accept or reject it, and 30 business days after payment becomes due to pay an accepted claim; these form terms must be distinguished from the North Carolina bulletin's regulatory standards.

The Texas prompt-payment bulletin sets regulatory standards of acknowledgment no later than 15 days after receipt, acceptance or rejection within 15 business days after all reasonably requested items, and payment of an accepted claim within 5 business days; it also bars conditioning an undisputed amount on resolution of a disputed amount.

The Texas HO-01-45 form sets different contractual claims-handling periods from the Texas bulletin: acknowledgment within 15 days, acceptance or rejection within 10 business days after requested items, and payment within 5 business days after acceptance notice.

The North Carolina HO-01-32 and Texas HO-01-45 forms permit the insurer to request a signed or signed-and-sworn proof of loss and supporting information without stating a numeric proof period in the cited claims-handling provisions, so the handler must use the operative form and applicable law rather than import a period from another jurisdiction or edition.
The North Carolina HO-01-32 form limits appraisal to the policy-permitted appraisal process and expressly excludes coverage, causation, and deductible applicability from the appraisal decision.

The Texas HO-01-45 form permits appraisal when the parties disagree about the amount of loss and requires an insured to participate when appraisal is properly requested, while its suit condition requires compliance with policy terms and commencement within two years after the cause of action accrues.
The North Carolina HO-01-32 suit condition requires an action against the insurer to be brought within three years after the date of loss, subject to compliance with the form's conditions.

Internal closure controls require the handler to resolve or appropriately transfer material coverage, payment, recovery, and complaint issues, verify payment and final-disposition communication, and reopen when new information requires further carrier action; catastrophe event closure does not end the handling obligations for remaining claims.
